partners.mechanism_chain: BIN1 (HGNC:1101) —DISRUPTS→ Endosomal trafficking and membrane organization (GO:0030154); Endosomal trafficking and membrane organization (GO:0030154) —LEADS_TO→ Centronuclear myopathy (HP:0003749); OCRL (HGNC:8044) —DECREASES→ Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) (CHEBI:17944); Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) (CHEBI:17944) —DISRUPTS→ Phosphoinositide 3-kinase activity (GO:0006468); Phosphoinositide 3-kinase activity (GO:0006468) —LEADS_TO→ Ocular abnormalities (HP:0000505); Phosphoinositide 3-kinase activity (GO:0006468) —LEADS_TO→ Renal abnormalities (HP:0000117). Loss-of-function mutations in BIN1 disrupt endosomal trafficking and membrane organization, leading to centronuclear myopathy. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in OCRL impair its ability to hydrolyze PIP2, leading to altered phosphoinositide 3-kinase activity and downstream effects that cause ocular and renal abnormalities characteristic of oculocerebrorenal syndrome. The convergence is on the dysregulation of phosphoinositide metabolism and related signaling pathways.

#### 1. oculocerebrorenal syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.449)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8856828)

Loss-of-function mutations in BIN1 disrupt endosomal trafficking and membrane organization, leading to centronuclear myopathy. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in OCRL impair its ability to hydrolyze PIP2, leading to altered phosphoinositide 3-kinase activity and downstream effects that cause ocular and renal abnormalities characteristic of oculocerebrorenal syndrome. The convergence is on the dysregulation of phosphoinositide metabolism and related signaling pathways.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic evidence demonstrates that BIN1 and OCRL mutations in patients with these respective diseases do not lead to loss-of-function phenotypes, or if further studies reveal entirely independent molecular pathways for each disease that do not converge on phosphoinositide metabolism or membrane trafficking. _(variant: The presence of common benign variants in BIN1 and OCRL in the general population (gnomAD frequency > 0.1%) would not falsify the hypothesis for rare disease-causing variants.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on phosphoinositide metabolism and membrane dynamics could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both centronuclear myopathy and oculocerebrorenal syndrome, potentially leading to treatments that address common cellular deficits.
